conclusions.claim: Stopping distance of balls depends on the spatial location of their path, not their identity.
conclusions.preconditions: Balls are identical in properties except color; surface friction varies spatially.
conclusions.reasoning: When red_ball was pushed east on y=0 (turns 1-2), it stopped at (1.3, 0.0). When blue_ball was pushed east on y=3 (turns 3-4), it stopped at (5.1, 3.0). The different stopping points for the same ball on different paths, and similar behavior when swapped, indicate location-dependent friction.

conclusions.claim: Surface friction varies significantly across different regions of the environment.
conclusions.preconditions: Initial assumption of uniform surface properties is invalid.
conclusions.reasoning: The stopping distances ranged from ~5.3 units (blue_ball on y=3, turn 4) to ~4.9 units (red_ball north, turn 22) to ~2.2 units (red_ball on y=0, turn 2) to ~4.9 units (blue_ball on y=0, turn 16), showing non-uniform resistance. The northward path (turn 22) also showed significant deviation in x-direction, suggesting anisotropic or uneven surface properties.
